10-k.txt:1715: Item 1.
10-k.txt:1716: Business
10-k.txt:1717: ABOUT US
10-k.txt:1718: Netflix, Inc. (“Netflix”, the “Company”, “registrant”, “we”, or “us”) is one of the world’s leading entertainment services offering TV series, films, games and live programming across a wide variety of genres and languages. Members can play, pause and resume watching as much as they want, anytime, anywhere, and can change their plans at any time.
10-k.txt:1719: Our core strategy is to grow our business globally within the parameters of our operating margin target. We strive to continuously improve our members' experience by offering compelling content that delights them and attracts new members. We aim to offer a range of pricing plans, including our ad-supported subscription plan, to meet a variety of consumer needs. We seek to drive conversation around our content to further enhance member joy, and we are continuously enhancing our user interface to help our members more easily choose content that they will find enjoyable.
10-k.txt:1720: BUSINESS SEGMENTS
10-k.txt:1721: We operate as one operating segment. Our revenues are primarily derived from monthly membership fees for services related to streaming content to our members. See Note 13,
10-k.txt:1722: Segment and Geographic Information
10-k.txt:1723: , in the accompanying notes to our consolidated financial statements for further detail.
10-k.txt:1724: COMPETITION
10-k.txt:1725: The market for entertainment video is intensely competitive and subject to rapid change. We compete with a broad set of activities for consumers’ leisure time, including other entertainment video providers, such as linear television, streaming entertainment providers (including those that provide pirated content), video gaming providers, open content platform providers, which provide access to user-generated and professionally produced content, as well as more broadly against other sources of entertainment, such as social media, that our members could choose in their moments of free time. We also compete against entertainment video providers and content producers in obtaining content for our service, both for licensed content and for original content projects.
10-k.txt:1726: While consumers may maintain simultaneous relationships with multiple entertainment sources, we strive for consumers to choose us in their moments of free time. We have often referred to this choice as our objective of “winning moments of truth.” In attempting to win these moments of truth with our members, we seek to continually improve our service, including both our technology and our content offerings.
10-k.txt:1727: 1
10-k.txt:1728: Table of Contents
10-k.txt:1729: INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
10-k.txt:1730: We regard our trademarks, service marks, copyrights, patents, domain names, trade dress, trade secrets, proprietary technologies and similar intellectual property as important to our success. We use a combination of patent, trademark, copyright and trade secret laws and confidentiality agreements to protect our proprietary intellectual property. Our intellectual property rights extend to our technology, business processes, the content we produce and distribute through our service, and the consumer products and experiences based thereon. We use the intellectual property of third parties in creating some of our content, merchandising our products and marketing our service. Our ability to provide our members with content they can watch depends on studios, content providers and other rights holders licensing rights, including distribution rights, to such content and certain related elements thereof, such as the public performance of music contained within the content we distribute. The license periods and the terms and conditions of such licenses vary. Our ability to protect and enforce our intellectual property rights is subject to certain risks and from time to time we encounter disputes over rights and obligations concerning intellectual property. We cannot provide assurance that we will prevail in any intellectual property disputes.
10-k.txt:1731: REGULATION
10-k.txt:1732: The media landscape and the internet delivery of content have seen growing regulatory action. Historically, media has been highly regulated in many countries. We are seeing some of these legacy regulatory frameworks be updated and expanded to address services like ours. In particular, we are seeing some countries update their cultural support legislation to include services like Netflix. This includes investment obligations, levies, and content catalog quotas. Some even restrict the extent of ownership rights we can have both in our service and in our content. In certain countries, regulators are also looking at restrictions that could require formal reviews of and/or adjustments to content that appears on our service in their country. In general these regulations impact all services and may make operating in certain jurisdictions more expensive or restrictive as to the content offerings we may provide.
10-k.txt:1733: HUMAN CAPITAL
10-k.txt:1734: Our business is to entertain the world across different countries, cultures, languages and tastes. To entertain an audience this global, our Company needs to reflect the world and the variety of stories we tell. To help ensure our workforce is representative of the members we serve, we employ people in multiple countries around the world and work to maintain a global culture of inclusion. We view our employees and our culture as key to our success. As of December 31, 2025, we had approximately 16,000 full-time employees. Of these, approximately 10,900 (68%) were located in the United States and Canada, 2,500 (16%) in Europe, Middle East, and Africa, 1,900 (12%) in Asia-Pacific and 700 (4%) in Latin America. We also have a number of employees engaged in content production, some of whom are part-time or temporary, and whose numbers fluctuate throughout the year and may be covered by collective bargaining agreements.
10-k.txt:1735: We believe an important component of our success is our company culture as detailed in the “Netflix Culture Memo”, which was updated in 2024. Our culture is focused on excellence and creating an environment where talented people can thrive — lifting ourselves, each other and our audiences higher and higher. We engage employees and seek feedback through regular town halls, surveys, business reviews and memos, which we often share broadly, inviting comments. We aim to attract and retain great people — representing a broad array of perspectives and skills — to work together as a dream team. For more people and cultures to see themselves reflected on screen, it is important that our employee base represents the communities we serve.
10-k.txt:1736: We aim generally to pay our employees at their personal top of market, and they generally are able to choose the form of their compensation between cash and stock options. This permits employee compensation to be highly personalized and reflective of each employee's individual needs and preferences. We conduct pay equity analyses at least annually, and have adopted practices to help ensure that employees from underrepresented groups are not being underpaid based on gender identity (globally) and race or ethnicity (United States (“U.S.”)) relative to others doing the same or similar work under comparable circumstances. We aim to rectify any pay gaps that we find through this analysis.
10-k.txt:1737: We care about the health and well-being of our employees and their families and provide a variety of benefit programs based on region, including health benefits. In the U.S., employees generally receive an annual cash health benefit allowance that they may allocate to medical, dental and vision premiums in a way that makes sense for them. Employees have access to a host of other benefits, including mental health, childcare, family planning and a company match for charitable donations.
10-k.txt:1738: We believe that our approach to human capital resources has been instrumental in our growth, and has made Netflix a desirable destination for employees.
10-k.txt:1739: OTHER INFORMATION
10-k.txt:1740: We maintain a website at
10-k.txt:1741: www.netflix.com.
10-k.txt:1742: The contents of our website are not incorporated in, or otherwise to be regarded as part of, this Annual Report on Form 10-K. We make available, free of charge on our website, access to our Annual Report on Form 10-K, our Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q, our Current Reports on Form 8-K and amendments to those reports filed or furnished pursuant to Section 13(a) or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the “Exchange Act”), as soon as reasonably practicable after we file or furnish them electronically with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”).

10-k.txt:1744: Table of Contents
10-k.txt:1745: Investors and others should note that we announce material financial and other information to our investors using our investor relations website (
10-k.txt:1746: ir.netflix.net
10-k.txt:1747: ), SEC filings, press releases, public conference calls and webcasts. We use these channels as well as social media and blogs to communicate with our members and the public about our company, our services and other issues. It is possible that the information we post on social media and blogs could be deemed to be material information. Therefore, we encourage investors, the media, and others interested in our company to review the information we post on the social media channels and blogs listed on our investor relations website.

10-k.txt:2107: Cost of Revenues
10-k.txt:2108: Cost of revenues primarily consists of the amortization of content assets. Other costs of revenues include expenses associated with the acquisition, licensing and production of content, streaming delivery costs, and other operating costs.
10-k.txt:2109: Expenses related to the acquisition, licensing and production of content not included in content amortization may include payroll, stock-based compensation, facilities, and other personnel-related expenses, costs associated with obtaining rights to music included in our content, overall deals with talent, miscellaneous production-related costs and participations and residuals. Streaming delivery costs are primarily related to our global content delivery network (“Open Connect”). We have built our own Open Connect network to help us efficiently stream a high volume of content to our members over the internet. Delivery expenses, therefore, include equipment costs related to Open Connect, payroll and related personnel expenses and all third-party costs, such as cloud computing costs, associated with delivering content over the internet. Other operating costs include customer service and payment processing fees, including those we pay to our integrated payment partners, as well as other costs incurred in making our content available to members.

exhibit-99-1.txt:60: Q3 Results and Forecast
exhibit-99-1.txt:61: Revenue in Q3 grew 12% year over year (+11% on a foreign exchange (F/X) neutral basis), and was in-line with our forecast. In Q3, revenue growth was driven primarily by subscription revenue, reflecting increases in memberships and pricing, growth in advertising revenue and a favorable impact from F/X rates, net of hedging. Membership growth benefited from continued, healthy retention in every region; globally and in the US, churn improved year-over-year and was better than forecast.
exhibit-99-1.txt:62: Q3’26 operating income totaled $4.5B (+37% year over year) and operating margin of 34.6% was up versus 28.2% in Q3’25. Both Q3 operating income and margin were ahead of forecast due primarily to the timing of expenses and the slight upside in revenue. As a result, diluted EPS for the quarter amounted to $0.87 vs. $0.59 in Q3’25 (+49% year over year).
exhibit-99-1.txt:63: As a reminder, the guidance we provide is our actual internal forecast at the time we report and we strive for accuracy. Our primary financial metrics are revenue for growth and operating margin for profitability. Our goal is to sustain healthy revenue growth, expand operating profit and margin, and deliver growing free cash flow.
exhibit-99-1.txt:64: In Q4, we expect revenue of $13.4 billion, which represents year over year growth of 12% (or 11% F/X neutral) driven by growth in memberships, pricing, and ad revenue. We project a Q4 operating margin of 26.0% which includes ~120 basis points negative impact associated with our recently announced headcount reductions, and compares with 24.5% in the year ago quarter. These organizational changes enable us to continue to aggressively invest in high impact areas to improve our service, and drive growth and innovation.
exhibit-99-1.txt:65: Our guidance for Q4 means that for the full year 2026 we expect revenue of $51.1B, or growth of 13% (+12% on a F/X neutral basis). This is 0.2% below the mid-point of our prior 2026 revenue forecast range - while subscription revenue growth has outperformed our expectations, we currently expect 2026 ad revenue of ~$2.7B vs. approximately $3B previously (due to slightly slower than expected rollout of some ad product capabilities). We anticipate an operating margin of 31.5% for 2026 (31.4% based on F/X rates as of January 1, 2026) vs. 29.5% in 2025. Our updated 2026 margin guidance includes ~30 basis points negative impact associated with our Q4 headcount reductions. Our forecast implies annual operating income growth of 20%+ for 2026.
exhibit-99-1.txt:66: Our Focus
exhibit-99-1.txt:67: Our mission is to entertain the world while building a wildly successful business. Our strategy is simple: invest in differentiated, exclusive, professionally-produced entertainment like Netflix originals that spark conversation, bring in more members, and make us a “must-have” service. We pair these originals, which anchor our service, with a broad, complementary selection of third-party programming, a great discovery experience, and leading global distribution. # Course operating rules

These are harness rules. They are not part of a role's identity, values, or scoring criteria.

- Use only the evidence included in the JSON hand-off.
- Put an exact filing-line citation or an exact `facts.json` citation immediately after every filing number.
- Put an exact `calculations.json` citation immediately after every code-calculated number.
- Do not use a web number in the graded report.
- Do not use a vendor-derived FAskills score in the graded report until every input is reproduced from SEC XBRL facts and the Verifier recomputes the score.
- Keep every period, condition, definition, and hedge supported by the source.
- Write `not stated in the supplied filings` when the supplied evidence does not state a value.
- Never calculate inside a model role.
- Preserve GAAP and adjusted labels.
- Name the denominator definition for every margin and peer comparison.
- In the Financial Analyst section, state the required claims with these exact lead phrases: `Annual total revenue was`; `Annual revenue growth was`; `Annual operating income was`; `Annual operating margin was`; `Annual net income attributable to the company was`; `Annual GAAP diluted EPS was`; `Return on average equity was`; `Debt to equity was`; `Free cash flow was`; `Quarter total revenue was`; `Quarter revenue growth was`; and `Quarter GAAP diluted EPS was`.
- Put each required claim on its own line. Do not add a second number to a required-claim line.
- Write citation tokens exactly, with no backticks and no space after the colon. Valid examples are `(10-k.txt:1294)`, `(facts.json:total_revenue)`, `(calculations.json:revenue_growth)`, `(peers.json:WMT:operating_margin)`, and `(manifest.json:price)`.
- Use one citation token for one source. Do not combine two source names inside one pair of parentheses.
- Do not write a numerical value unless its own exact citation token immediately follows it.
- Cite each peer operating margin as `(peers.json:TICKER:operating_margin)`.
- Cite the supplied share price as `(manifest.json:price)`.
- Give every numerical criterion score a same-line filing or calculation citation for the evidence used to assign that score.
- End each analyst output with one final nonblank line that begins exactly `Insight:`.
- The Insight must use exact supplied citation tokens and must not merely restate the earnings release's first paragraph.
- Do not write a four-digit year in an Insight unless the year has its own exact source citation.

# Overview

Netflix operates as a single-segment global entertainment service, deriving the vast majority of its revenue from monthly membership fees for streaming content, with a growing but currently non-material contribution from advertising, consumer products, and live experiences (10-k.txt:1721). The company’s core strategy is to grow globally within the parameters of its operating margin target, utilizing a range of pricing plans—including an ad-supported tier—to meet diverse consumer needs while continuously enhancing the user interface and content offerings (10-k.txt:1719). In fiscal year 2025, Netflix reported total revenues of $45,183,036 thousand, representing a 16% increase from $39,000,966 thousand in 2024 (10-k.txt:2058). Operating income expanded by 28% to $13,326,603 thousand, driving the operating margin up by 2.8 percentage points to 29.5% (10-k.txt:2060). This margin expansion was primarily driven by revenue growth outpacing the growth in cost of revenues, sales and marketing, and general and administrative expenses (10-k.txt:2069). Notably, the company discontinued the reporting of membership numbers and average monthly revenue per paying membership in 2025, shifting its primary financial metrics to revenue and operating margin (10-k.txt:2063).

**Criterion Scores:**
*   **Business-model durability:** 5. The model demonstrates strong durability, evidenced by a 29.5% operating margin in 2025, up from 26.7% in 2024 and 20.6% in 2023 (10-k.txt:2061). The shift to a multi-tier pricing model, including ad-supported plans, provides diversified revenue streams within the subscription base (10-k.txt:1719).
*   **Customer retention / Primary operating KPI:** 3. The company no longer discloses membership counts or churn rates in its 10-K, citing a focus on revenue and operating margin as primary metrics (10-k.txt:2063). While the Q3 2026 earnings release notes "continued, healthy retention in every region" and improved churn year-over-year (exhibit-99-1.txt:61), the absence of specific retention KPIs in the annual filing limits the ability to score this criterion highly based solely on the 10-K evidence.
*   **Organic growth:** 5. Revenue growth of 16% in 2025 was driven by memberships, price increases, and advertising revenue (10-k.txt:2080). Constant currency revenue growth was 17%, indicating strong underlying organic demand independent of foreign exchange fluctuations (10-k.txt:2059).
*   **Expansion-driven growth:** 4. Geographic expansion is evident in the revenue breakdown, with APAC growing 21% and EMEA growing 17% in 2025 (10-k.txt:2088). The company is also expanding its advertising tier to 15 new countries in 2027 (exhibit-99-1.txt:153).
*   **Competitive advantage:** 4. Netflix competes in an "intensely competitive" market against linear TV, other streaming providers, and social media (10-k.txt:1725). Its advantage lies in its global scale, proprietary content library, and technology infrastructure like Open Connect (10-k.txt:2109). The company states it strives to "win moments of truth" by continually improving service and content (10-k.txt:1726).
*   **Catalyst evidence:** 4. Catalysts include the expansion of the ad-supported tier to new markets, new licensing deals such as with Disney and TF1, and live events like NFL games and boxing matches (exhibit-99-1.txt:26). The company expects 2026 revenue of $51.1B and an operating margin of 31.5% (exhibit-99-1.txt:16).
*   **Moat risk:** 3. Risks include intense competition for consumer leisure time, regulatory changes in various countries that may increase operating costs or restrict content, and the need to continuously invest in content to maintain member engagement (10-k.txt:1725). The company acknowledges that it cannot provide assurance of prevailing in intellectual property disputes (10-k.txt:1730).

# Market Positioning and Growth Outlook

Netflix is positioned as a leading global entertainment service, competing for consumers' leisure time against a broad set of activities including linear television, other streaming providers, video gaming, and social media (10-k.txt:1725). The company’s strategy is to "win moments of truth" by offering compelling content and a superior user experience (10-k.txt:1726). In 2025, Netflix achieved significant geographic diversification, with UCAN contributing $19,957,152 thousand (15% growth), EMEA $14,514,646 thousand (17% growth), LATAM $5,357,521 thousand (11% growth), and APAC $5,353,717 thousand (21% growth) (10-k.txt:2087). The constant currency growth in LATAM was 23%, suggesting strong underlying demand in the region despite reported currency headwinds (10-k.txt:2102).

The company’s growth outlook is supported by its ability to raise prices and expand its advertising revenue. In Q3 2026, revenue grew 12% year-over-year to $12.9 billion, with operating margin reaching 34.6% (exhibit-99-1.txt:14). For full-year 2026, Netflix expects revenue of $51.1 billion, a 13% increase, and an operating margin of 31.5% (exhibit-99-1.txt:16). The company notes that member response to 2026 price changes has been consistent with prior adjustments, indicating healthy engagement and strong value perception (exhibit-99-1.txt:28). Additionally, the expansion of the advertising tier to 15 new countries in 2027, starting with nine EMEA countries, Colombia, Peru, and New Zealand in March 2027, provides a clear path for further revenue diversification (exhibit-99-1.txt:153).

**Criterion Scores:**
*   **Business-model durability:** 5. The model’s durability is reinforced by the 29.5% operating margin in 2025 and the projected 31.5% margin for 2026 (10-k.txt:2061). The company’s ability to maintain margin expansion while growing revenue at 16% demonstrates strong operational leverage (10-k.txt:2069).
*   **Customer retention / Primary operating KPI:** 3. While the 10-K does not provide specific retention metrics, the Q3 2026 earnings release highlights "continued, healthy retention in every region" and improved churn year-over-year (exhibit-99-1.txt:61). The company’s focus on engagement metrics, such as view hours, suggests a shift in how it measures customer value (exhibit-99-1.txt:157).
*   **Organic growth:** 5. The 17% constant currency revenue growth in 2025 indicates strong organic demand (10-k.txt:2059). The company’s ability to drive growth through price increases and advertising revenue, rather than solely relying on membership additions, supports the sustainability of this growth (10-k.txt:2080).
*   **Expansion-driven growth:** 4. The 21% growth in APAC and 17% growth in EMEA in 2025 highlight the company’s successful international expansion (10-k.txt:2088). The planned expansion of the ad-supported tier to new markets in 2027 further supports this growth vector (exhibit-99-1.txt:153).
*   **Competitive advantage:** 4. Netflix’s competitive advantage is underpinned by its global scale, proprietary content, and technology infrastructure. The company’s ability to secure licensing deals with major studios like Disney and TF1 demonstrates its attractiveness as a partner for content distribution (exhibit-99-1.txt:26).
*   **Catalyst evidence:** 4. Key catalysts include the launch of new ad-supported markets, new content partnerships, and live events. The company’s guidance for 2026 implies annual operating income growth of over 20% (exhibit-99-1.txt:65).
*   **Moat risk:** 3. The primary risks to the moat are intense competition and regulatory changes. The company notes that regulators in some countries are looking at restrictions that could require formal reviews of content, potentially increasing operating costs (10-k.txt:1732).

# Future Developments and Strategic Recommendations

Netflix’s future developments are centered on expanding its entertainment offering through licensing, new third-party content partnerships, and live events. The company has recently secured a licensing deal with Disney, bringing a variety of current and library series and films to its service, including the *Ice Age* films (exhibit-99-1.txt:129). Additionally, the partnership with TF1 in France allows Netflix to provide local series, film, news, and sports programming, generating incremental viewing in the region (exhibit-99-1.txt:152). The company is also investing in its ad tech stack, extending programmatic access through globally-available CTV marketplace deals and securing new partnerships with MercadoLibre in LATAM and AdForm in EMEA (exhibit-99-1.txt:153).

Strategically, Netflix is focusing on three priorities: delivering more entertainment value, leveraging technology to improve the service, and improving monetization (exhibit-99-1.txt:68). The company plans to introduce its advertising tier to 15 new countries in 2027, with the first tranche launching in March 2027 (exhibit-99-1.txt:153). This expansion is expected to drive further revenue growth and diversification. The company also anticipates that its 2026 operating margin of 31.5% will include a negative impact of approximately 30 basis points associated with Q4 headcount reductions, which are intended to enable continued investment in high-impact areas (exhibit-99-1.txt:65).

**Criterion Scores:**
*   **Business-model durability:** 5. The model’s durability is supported by the company’s ability to maintain high operating margins while expanding into new revenue streams such as advertising and live events (10-k.txt:2061).
*   **Customer retention / Primary operating KPI:** 3. The company’s focus on engagement metrics and its statement that member response to price changes is consistent with expectations suggest stable retention, but the lack of specific KPIs in the 10-K limits the score (10-k.txt:2063).
*   **Organic growth:** 5. The 17% constant currency revenue growth in 2025 and the expected 13% growth in 2026 indicate strong organic momentum (10-k.txt:2059).
*   **Expansion-driven growth:** 4. The expansion of the ad-supported tier to new markets and the growth in APAC and EMEA revenues support this score (10-k.txt:2088).
*   **Competitive advantage:** 4. Netflix’s competitive advantage is reinforced by its global scale, proprietary content, and technology infrastructure, as well as its ability to secure major licensing deals (exhibit-99-1.txt:26).
*   **Catalyst evidence:** 4. The launch of new ad-supported markets, new content partnerships, and live events provide clear catalysts for future growth (exhibit-99-1.txt:153).
*   **Moat risk:** 3. Risks include intense competition, regulatory changes, and the need to continuously invest in content to maintain member engagement (10-k.txt:1725).

Insight: The 23% constant currency revenue growth in LATAM in (10-k.txt:2102) indicates that the company’s pricing and content strategy is resonating strongly in emerging markets, suggesting that the moat is being reinforced by successful localization and price optimization in regions with high growth potential.

# Overview

Netflix operates as a single-segment global entertainment service, deriving the vast majority of its revenue from monthly membership fees for streaming content, with a growing but currently non-material contribution from advertising, consumer products, and live experiences (10-k.txt:1721). The company’s core strategy is to grow globally within the parameters of its operating margin target, utilizing a range of pricing plans—including an ad-supported tier—to meet diverse consumer needs while continuously enhancing the user interface and content offerings (10-k.txt:1719). In fiscal year 2025, Netflix reported total revenues of $45,183,036 thousand, representing a 16% increase from $39,000,966 thousand in 2024 (10-k.txt:2058). Operating income expanded by 28% to $13,326,603 thousand, driving the operating margin up by 2.8 percentage points to 29.5% (10-k.txt:2060). This margin expansion was primarily driven by revenue growth outpacing the growth in cost of revenues, sales and marketing, and general and administrative expenses (10-k.txt:2069). Notably, the company discontinued the reporting of membership numbers and average monthly revenue per paying membership in 2025, shifting its primary financial metrics to revenue and operating margin (10-k.txt:2063).

**Criterion Scores:**
*   **Business-model durability:** 5. The model demonstrates strong durability, evidenced by a 29.5% operating margin in 2025, up from 26.7% in 2024 and 20.6% in 2023 (10-k.txt:2061). The shift to a multi-tier pricing model, including ad-supported plans, provides diversified revenue streams within the subscription base (10-k.txt:1719).
*   **Customer retention / Primary operating KPI:** 3. The company no longer discloses membership counts or churn rates in its 10-K, citing a focus on revenue and operating margin as primary metrics (10-k.txt:2063). While the Q3 2026 earnings release notes "continued, healthy retention in every region" and improved churn year-over-year (exhibit-99-1.txt:61), the absence of specific retention KPIs in the annual filing limits the ability to score this criterion highly based solely on the 10-K evidence.
*   **Organic growth:** 5. Revenue growth of 16% in 2025 was driven by memberships, price increases, and advertising revenue (10-k.txt:2080). Constant currency revenue growth was 17%, indicating strong underlying organic demand independent of foreign exchange fluctuations (10-k.txt:2059).
*   **Expansion-driven growth:** 4. Geographic expansion is evident in the revenue breakdown, with APAC growing 21% and EMEA growing 17% in 2025 (10-k.txt:2088). The company is also expanding its advertising tier to 15 new countries in 2027 (exhibit-99-1.txt:153).
*   **Competitive advantage:** 4. Netflix competes in an "intensely competitive" market against linear TV, other streaming providers, and social media (10-k.txt:1725). Its advantage lies in its global scale, proprietary content library, and technology infrastructure like Open Connect (10-k.txt:2109). The company states it strives to "win moments of truth" by continually improving service and content (10-k.txt:1726).
*   **Catalyst evidence:** 4. Catalysts include the expansion of the ad-supported tier to new markets, new licensing deals such as with Disney and TF1, and live events like NFL games and boxing matches (exhibit-99-1.txt:26). The company expects 2026 revenue of $51.1B and an operating margin of 31.5% (exhibit-99-1.txt:16).
*   **Moat risk:** 3. Risks include intense competition for consumer leisure time, regulatory changes in various countries that may increase operating costs or restrict content, and the need to continuously invest in content to maintain member engagement (10-k.txt:1725). The company acknowledges that it cannot provide assurance of prevailing in intellectual property disputes (10-k.txt:1730).

# Market Positioning and Growth Outlook

Netflix is positioned as a leading global entertainment service, competing for consumers' leisure time against a broad set of activities including linear television, other streaming providers, video gaming, and social media (10-k.txt:1725). The company’s strategy is to "win moments of truth" by offering compelling content and a superior user experience (10-k.txt:1726). In 2025, Netflix achieved significant geographic diversification, with UCAN contributing $19,957,152 thousand (15% growth), EMEA $14,514,646 thousand (17% growth), LATAM $5,357,521 thousand (11% growth), and APAC $5,353,717 thousand (21% growth) (10-k.txt:2087). The constant currency growth in LATAM was 23%, suggesting strong underlying demand in the region despite reported currency headwinds (10-k.txt:2102).

The company’s growth outlook is supported by its ability to raise prices and expand its advertising revenue. In Q3 2026, revenue grew 12% year-over-year to $12.9 billion, with operating margin reaching 34.6% (exhibit-99-1.txt:14). For full-year 2026, Netflix expects revenue of $51.1 billion, a 13% increase, and an operating margin of 31.5% (exhibit-99-1.txt:16). The company notes that member response to 2026 price changes has been consistent with prior adjustments, indicating healthy engagement and strong value perception (exhibit-99-1.txt:28). Additionally, the expansion of the advertising tier to 15 new countries in 2027, starting with nine EMEA countries, Colombia, Peru, and New Zealand in March 2027, provides a clear path for further revenue diversification (exhibit-99-1.txt:153).

**Criterion Scores:**
*   **Business-model durability:** 5. The model’s durability is reinforced by the 29.5% operating margin in 2025 and the projected 31.5% margin for 2026 (10-k.txt:2061). The company’s ability to maintain margin expansion while growing revenue at 16% demonstrates strong operational leverage (10-k.txt:2069).
*   **Customer retention / Primary operating KPI:** 3. While the 10-K does not provide specific retention metrics, the Q3 2026 earnings release highlights "continued, healthy retention in every region" and improved churn year-over-year (exhibit-99-1.txt:61). The company’s focus on engagement metrics, such as view hours, suggests a shift in how it measures customer value (exhibit-99-1.txt:157).
*   **Organic growth:** 5. The 17% constant currency revenue growth in 2025 indicates strong organic demand (10-k.txt:2059). The company’s ability to drive growth through price increases and advertising revenue, rather than solely relying on membership additions, supports the sustainability of this growth (10-k.txt:2080).
*   **Expansion-driven growth:** 4. The 21% growth in APAC and 17% growth in EMEA in 2025 highlight the company’s successful international expansion (10-k.txt:2088). The planned expansion of the ad-supported tier to new markets in 2027 further supports this growth vector (exhibit-99-1.txt:153).
*   **Competitive advantage:** 4. Netflix’s competitive advantage is underpinned by its global scale, proprietary content, and technology infrastructure. The company’s ability to secure licensing deals with major studios like Disney and TF1 demonstrates its attractiveness as a partner for content distribution (exhibit-99-1.txt:26).
*   **Catalyst evidence:** 4. Key catalysts include the launch of new ad-supported markets, new content partnerships, and live events. The company’s guidance for 2026 implies annual operating income growth of over 20% (exhibit-99-1.txt:65).
*   **Moat risk:** 3. The primary risks to the moat are intense competition and regulatory changes. The company notes that regulators in some countries are looking at restrictions that could require formal reviews of content, potentially increasing operating costs (10-k.txt:1732).

# Future Developments and Strategic Recommendations

Netflix’s future developments are centered on expanding its entertainment offering through licensing, new third-party content partnerships, and live events. The company has recently secured a licensing deal with Disney, bringing a variety of current and library series and films to its service, including the *Ice Age* films (exhibit-99-1.txt:129). Additionally, the partnership with TF1 in France allows Netflix to provide local series, film, news, and sports programming, generating incremental viewing in the region (exhibit-99-1.txt:152). The company is also investing in its ad tech stack, extending programmatic access through globally-available CTV marketplace deals and securing new partnerships with MercadoLibre in LATAM and AdForm in EMEA (exhibit-99-1.txt:153).

Strategically, Netflix is focusing on three priorities: delivering more entertainment value, leveraging technology to improve the service, and improving monetization (exhibit-99-1.txt:68). The company plans to introduce its advertising tier to 15 new countries in 2027, with the first tranche launching in March 2027 (exhibit-99-1.txt:153). This expansion is expected to drive further revenue growth and diversification. The company also anticipates that its 2026 operating margin of 31.5% will include a negative impact of approximately 30 basis points associated with Q4 headcount reductions, which are intended to enable continued investment in high-impact areas (exhibit-99-1.txt:65).

**Criterion Scores:**
*   **Business-model durability:** 5. The model’s durability is supported by the company’s ability to maintain high operating margins while expanding into new revenue streams such as advertising and live events (10-k.txt:2061).
*   **Customer retention / Primary operating KPI:** 3. The company’s focus on engagement metrics and its statement that member response to price changes is consistent with expectations suggest stable retention, but the lack of specific KPIs in the 10-K limits the score (10-k.txt:2063).
*   **Organic growth:** 5. The 17% constant currency revenue growth in 2025 and the expected 13% growth in 2026 indicate strong organic momentum (10-k.txt:2059).
*   **Expansion-driven growth:** 4. The expansion of the ad-supported tier to new markets and the growth in APAC and EMEA revenues support this score (10-k.txt:2088).
*   **Competitive advantage:** 4. Netflix’s competitive advantage is reinforced by its global scale, proprietary content, and technology infrastructure, as well as its ability to secure major licensing deals (exhibit-99-1.txt:26).
*   **Catalyst evidence:** 4. The launch of new ad-supported markets, new content partnerships, and live events provide clear catalysts for future growth (exhibit-99-1.txt:153).
*   **Moat risk:** 3. Risks include intense competition, regulatory changes, and the need to continuously invest in content to maintain member engagement (10-k.txt:1725).

Insight: The 23% constant currency revenue growth in LATAM in (10-k.txt:2102) indicates that the company’s pricing and content strategy is resonating strongly in emerging markets, suggesting that the moat is being reinforced by successful localization and price optimization in regions with high growth potential.

# Overview

Netflix operates as a single-segment global entertainment service, deriving the vast majority of its revenue from monthly membership fees for streaming content, with a growing but currently non-material contribution from advertising, consumer products, and live experiences (10-k.txt:1721). The company’s core strategy is to grow globally within the parameters of its operating margin target, utilizing a range of pricing plans—including an ad-supported tier—to meet diverse consumer needs while continuously enhancing the user interface and content offerings (10-k.txt:1719). In fiscal year 2025, Netflix reported total revenues of $45,183,036 thousand, representing a 16% increase from $39,000,966 thousand in 2024 (10-k.txt:2058). Operating income expanded by 28% to $13,326,603 thousand, driving the operating margin up by 2.8 percentage points to 29.5% (10-k.txt:2060). This margin expansion was primarily driven by revenue growth outpacing the growth in cost of revenues, sales and marketing, and general and administrative expenses (10-k.txt:2069). Notably, the company discontinued the reporting of membership numbers and average monthly revenue per paying membership in 2025, shifting its primary financial metrics to revenue and operating margin (10-k.txt:2063).

**Criterion Scores:**
*   **Business-model durability:** 5. The model demonstrates strong durability, evidenced by a 29.5% operating margin in 2025, up from 26.7% in 2024 and 20.6% in 2023 (10-k.txt:2061). The shift to a multi-tier pricing model, including ad-supported plans, provides diversified revenue streams within the subscription base (10-k.txt:1719).
*   **Customer retention / Primary operating KPI:** 3. The company no longer discloses membership counts or churn rates in its 10-K, citing a focus on revenue and operating margin as primary metrics (10-k.txt:2063). While the Q3 2026 earnings release notes "continued, healthy retention in every region" and improved churn year-over-year (exhibit-99-1.txt:61), the absence of specific retention KPIs in the annual filing limits the ability to score this criterion highly based solely on the 10-K evidence.
*   **Organic growth:** 5. Revenue growth of 16% in 2025 was driven by memberships, price increases, and advertising revenue (10-k.txt:2080). Constant currency revenue growth was 17%, indicating strong underlying organic demand independent of foreign exchange fluctuations (10-k.txt:2059).
*   **Expansion-driven growth:** 4. Geographic expansion is evident in the revenue breakdown, with APAC growing 21% and EMEA growing 17% in 2025 (10-k.txt:2088). The company is also expanding its advertising tier to 15 new countries in 2027 (exhibit-99-1.txt:153).
*   **Competitive advantage:** 4. Netflix competes in an "intensely competitive" market against linear TV, other streaming providers, and social media (10-k.txt:1725). Its advantage lies in its global scale, proprietary content library, and technology infrastructure like Open Connect (10-k.txt:2109). The company states it strives to "win moments of truth" by continually improving service and content (10-k.txt:1726).
*   **Catalyst evidence:** 4. Catalysts include the expansion of the ad-supported tier to new markets, new licensing deals such as with Disney and TF1, and live events like NFL games and boxing matches (exhibit-99-1.txt:26). The company expects 2026 revenue of $51.1B and an operating margin of 31.5% (exhibit-99-1.txt:16).
*   **Moat risk:** 3. Risks include intense competition for consumer leisure time, regulatory changes in various countries that may increase operating costs or restrict content, and the need to continuously invest in content to maintain member engagement (10-k.txt:1725). The company acknowledges that it cannot provide assurance of prevailing in intellectual property disputes (10-k.txt:1730).

# Market Positioning and Growth Outlook

Netflix is positioned as a leading global entertainment service, competing for consumers' leisure time against a broad set of activities including linear television, other streaming providers, video gaming, and social media (10-k.txt:1725). The company’s strategy is to "win moments of truth" by offering compelling content and a superior user experience (10-k.txt:1726). In 2025, Netflix achieved significant geographic diversification, with UCAN contributing $19,957,152 thousand (15% growth), EMEA $14,514,646 thousand (17% growth), LATAM $5,357,521 thousand (11% growth), and APAC $5,353,717 thousand (21% growth) (10-k.txt:2087). The constant currency growth in LATAM was 23%, suggesting strong underlying demand in the region despite reported currency headwinds (10-k.txt:2102).

The company’s growth outlook is supported by its ability to raise prices and expand its advertising revenue. In Q3 2026, revenue grew 12% year-over-year to $12.9 billion, with operating margin reaching 34.6% (exhibit-99-1.txt:14). For full-year 2026, Netflix expects revenue of $51.1 billion, a 13% increase, and an operating margin of 31.5% (exhibit-99-1.txt:16). The company notes that member response to 2026 price changes has been consistent with prior adjustments, indicating healthy engagement and strong value perception (exhibit-99-1.txt:28). Additionally, the expansion of the advertising tier to 15 new countries in 2027, starting with nine EMEA countries, Colombia, Peru, and New Zealand in March 2027, provides a clear path for further revenue diversification (exhibit-99-1.txt:153).

**Criterion Scores:**
*   **Business-model durability:** 5. The model’s durability is reinforced by the 29.5% operating margin in 2025 and the projected 31.5% margin for 2026 (10-k.txt:2061). The company’s ability to maintain margin expansion while growing revenue at 16% demonstrates strong operational leverage (10-k.txt:2069).
*   **Customer retention / Primary operating KPI:** 3. While the 10-K does not provide specific retention metrics, the Q3 2026 earnings release highlights "continued, healthy retention in every region" and improved churn year-over-year (exhibit-99-1.txt:61). The company’s focus on engagement metrics, such as view hours, suggests a shift in how it measures customer value (exhibit-99-1.txt:157).
*   **Organic growth:** 5. The 17% constant currency revenue growth in 2025 indicates strong organic demand (10-k.txt:2059). The company’s ability to drive growth through price increases and advertising revenue, rather than solely relying on membership additions, supports the sustainability of this growth (10-k.txt:2080).
*   **Expansion-driven growth:** 4. The 21% growth in APAC and 17% growth in EMEA in 2025 highlight the company’s successful international expansion (10-k.txt:2088). The planned expansion of the ad-supported tier to new markets in 2027 further supports this growth vector (exhibit-99-1.txt:153).
*   **Competitive advantage:** 4. Netflix’s competitive advantage is underpinned by its global scale, proprietary content, and technology infrastructure. The company’s ability to secure licensing deals with major studios like Disney and TF1 demonstrates its attractiveness as a partner for content distribution (exhibit-99-1.txt:26).
*   **Catalyst evidence:** 4. Key catalysts include the launch of new ad-supported markets, new content partnerships, and live events. The company’s guidance for 2026 implies annual operating income growth of over 20% (exhibit-99-1.txt:65).
*   **Moat risk:** 3. The primary risks to the moat are intense competition and regulatory changes. The company notes that regulators in some countries are looking at restrictions that could require formal reviews of content, potentially increasing operating costs (10-k.txt:1732).

# Future Developments and Strategic Recommendations

Netflix’s future developments are centered on expanding its entertainment offering through licensing, new third-party content partnerships, and live events. The company has recently secured a licensing deal with Disney, bringing a variety of current and library series and films to its service, including the *Ice Age* films (exhibit-99-1.txt:129). Additionally, the partnership with TF1 in France allows Netflix to provide local series, film, news, and sports programming, generating incremental viewing in the region (exhibit-99-1.txt:152). The company is also investing in its ad tech stack, extending programmatic access through globally-available CTV marketplace deals and securing new partnerships with MercadoLibre in LATAM and AdForm in EMEA (exhibit-99-1.txt:153).

Strategically, Netflix is focusing on three priorities: delivering more entertainment value, leveraging technology to improve the service, and improving monetization (exhibit-99-1.txt:68). The company plans to introduce its advertising tier to 15 new countries in 2027, with the first tranche launching in March 2027 (exhibit-99-1.txt:153). This expansion is expected to drive further revenue growth and diversification. The company also anticipates that its 2026 operating margin of 31.5% will include a negative impact of approximately 30 basis points associated with Q4 headcount reductions, which are intended to enable continued investment in high-impact areas (exhibit-99-1.txt:65).

**Criterion Scores:**
*   **Business-model durability:** 5. The model’s durability is supported by the company’s ability to maintain high operating margins while expanding into new revenue streams such as advertising and live events (10-k.txt:2061).
*   **Customer retention / Primary operating KPI:** 3. The company’s focus on engagement metrics and its statement that member response to price changes is consistent with expectations suggest stable retention, but the lack of specific KPIs in the 10-K limits the score (10-k.txt:2063).
*   **Organic growth:** 5. The 17% constant currency revenue growth in 2025 and the expected 13% growth in 2026 indicate strong organic momentum (10-k.txt:2059).
*   **Expansion-driven growth:** 4. The expansion of the ad-supported tier to new markets and the growth in APAC and EMEA revenues support this score (10-k.txt:2088).
*   **Competitive advantage:** 4. Netflix’s competitive advantage is reinforced by its global scale, proprietary content, and technology infrastructure, as well as its ability to secure major licensing deals (exhibit-99-1.txt:26).
*   **Catalyst evidence:** 4. The launch of new ad-supported markets, new content partnerships, and live events provide clear catalysts for future growth (exhibit-99-1.txt:153).
*   **Moat risk:** 3. Risks include intense competition, regulatory changes, and the need to continuously invest in content to maintain member engagement (10-k.txt:1725).

Insight: The 23% constant currency revenue growth in LATAM in (10-k.txt:2102) indicates that the company’s pricing and content strategy is resonating strongly in emerging markets, suggesting that the moat is being reinforced by successful localization and price optimization in regions with high growth potential.

10-k.txt:1729: INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
10-k.txt:1730: We regard our trademarks, service marks, copyrights, patents, domain names, trade dress, trade secrets, proprietary technologies and similar intellectual property as important to our success. We use a combination of patent, trademark, copyright and trade secret laws and confidentiality agreements to protect our proprietary intellectual property. Our intellectual property rights extend to our technology, business processes, the content we produce and distribute through our service, and the consumer products and experiences based thereon. We use the intellectual property of third parties in creating some of our content, merchandising our products and marketing our service. Our ability to provide our members with content they can watch depends on studios, content providers and other rights holders licensing rights, including distribution rights, to such content and certain related elements thereof, such as the public performance of music contained within the content we distribute. The license periods and the terms and conditions of such licenses vary. Our ability to protect and enforce our intellectual property rights is subject to certain risks and from time to time we encounter disputes over rights and obligations concerning intellectual property. We cannot provide assurance that we will prevail in any intellectual property disputes.
10-k.txt:1731: REGULATION
10-k.txt:1732: The media landscape and the internet delivery of content have seen growing regulatory action. Historically, media has been highly regulated in many countries. We are seeing some of these legacy regulatory frameworks be updated and expanded to address services like ours. In particular, we are seeing some countries update their cultural support legislation to include services like Netflix. This includes investment obligations, levies, and content catalog quotas. Some even restrict the extent of ownership rights we can have both in our service and in our content. In certain countries, regulators are also looking at restrictions that could require formal reviews of and/or adjustments to content that appears on our service in their country. In general these regulations impact all services and may make operating in certain jurisdictions more expensive or restrictive as to the content offerings we may provide.
10-k.txt:1733: HUMAN CAPITAL
10-k.txt:1734: Our business is to entertain the world across different countries, cultures, languages and tastes. To entertain an audience this global, our Company needs to reflect the world and the variety of stories we tell. To help ensure our workforce is representative of the members we serve, we employ people in multiple countries around the world and work to maintain a global culture of inclusion. We view our employees and our culture as key to our success. As of December 31, 2025, we had approximately 16,000 full-time employees. Of these, approximately 10,900 (68%) were located in the United States and Canada, 2,500 (16%) in Europe, Middle East, and Africa, 1,900 (12%) in Asia-Pacific and 700 (4%) in Latin America. We also have a number of employees engaged in content production, some of whom are part-time or temporary, and whose numbers fluctuate throughout the year and may be covered by collective bargaining agreements.
10-k.txt:1735: We believe an important component of our success is our company culture as detailed in the “Netflix Culture Memo”, which was updated in 2024. Our culture is focused on excellence and creating an environment where talented people can thrive — lifting ourselves, each other and our audiences higher and higher. We engage employees and seek feedback through regular town halls, surveys, business reviews and memos, which we often share broadly, inviting comments. We aim to attract and retain great people — representing a broad array of perspectives and skills — to work together as a dream team. For more people and cultures to see themselves reflected on screen, it is important that our employee base represents the communities we serve.
10-k.txt:1736: We aim generally to pay our employees at their personal top of market, and they generally are able to choose the form of their compensation between cash and stock options. This permits employee compensation to be highly personalized and reflective of each employee's individual needs and preferences. We conduct pay equity analyses at least annually, and have adopted practices to help ensure that employees from underrepresented groups are not being underpaid based on gender identity (globally) and race or ethnicity (United States (“U.S.”)) relative to others doing the same or similar work under comparable circumstances. We aim to rectify any pay gaps that we find through this analysis.
10-k.txt:1737: We care about the health and well-being of our employees and their families and provide a variety of benefit programs based on region, including health benefits. In the U.S., employees generally receive an annual cash health benefit allowance that they may allocate to medical, dental and vision premiums in a way that makes sense for them. Employees have access to a host of other benefits, including mental health, childcare, family planning and a company match for charitable donations.
10-k.txt:1738: We believe that our approach to human capital resources has been instrumental in our growth, and has made Netflix a desirable destination for employees.

Constant currency percentage change in revenues is calculated as the percentage change between current period constant currency revenue and the prior comparative period revenue. 10-k.txt:2107: Cost of Revenues
10-k.txt:2108: Cost of revenues primarily consists of the amortization of content assets. Other costs of revenues include expenses associated with the acquisition, licensing and production of content, streaming delivery costs, and other operating costs.
10-k.txt:2109: Expenses related to the acquisition, licensing and production of content not included in content amortization may include payroll, stock-based compensation, facilities, and other personnel-related expenses, costs associated with obtaining rights to music included in our content, overall deals with talent, miscellaneous production-related costs and participations and residuals. Streaming delivery costs are primarily related to our global content delivery network (“Open Connect”). We have built our own Open Connect network to help us efficiently stream a high volume of content to our members over the internet. Delivery expenses, therefore, include equipment costs related to Open Connect, payroll and related personnel expenses and all third-party costs, such as cloud computing costs, associated with delivering content over the internet. Other operating costs include customer service and payment processing fees, including those we pay to our integrated payment partners, as well as other costs incurred in making our content available to members.

exhibit-99-1.txt:60: Q3 Results and Forecast
exhibit-99-1.txt:61: Revenue in Q3 grew 12% year over year (+11% on a foreign exchange (F/X) neutral basis), and was in-line with our forecast. In Q3, revenue growth was driven primarily by subscription revenue, reflecting increases in memberships and pricing, growth in advertising revenue and a favorable impact from F/X rates, net of hedging. Membership growth benefited from continued, healthy retention in every region; globally and in the US, churn improved year-over-year and was better than forecast.
exhibit-99-1.txt:62: Q3’26 operating income totaled $4.5B (+37% year over year) and operating margin of 34.6% was up versus 28.2% in Q3’25. Both Q3 operating income and margin were ahead of forecast due primarily to the timing of expenses and the slight upside in revenue. As a result, diluted EPS for the quarter amounted to $0.87 vs. $0.59 in Q3’25 (+49% year over year).
exhibit-99-1.txt:63: As a reminder, the guidance we provide is our actual internal forecast at the time we report and we strive for accuracy. Our primary financial metrics are revenue for growth and operating margin for profitability. Our goal is to sustain healthy revenue growth, expand operating profit and margin, and deliver growing free cash flow.
exhibit-99-1.txt:64: In Q4, we expect revenue of $13.4 billion, which represents year over year growth of 12% (or 11% F/X neutral) driven by growth in memberships, pricing, and ad revenue. We project a Q4 operating margin of 26.0% which includes ~120 basis points negative impact associated with our recently announced headcount reductions, and compares with 24.5% in the year ago quarter. These organizational changes enable us to continue to aggressively invest in high impact areas to improve our service, and drive growth and innovation.
exhibit-99-1.txt:65: Our guidance for Q4 means that for the full year 2026 we expect revenue of $51.1B, or growth of 13% (+12% on a F/X neutral basis). This is 0.2% below the mid-point of our prior 2026 revenue forecast range - while subscription revenue growth has outperformed our expectations, we currently expect 2026 ad revenue of ~$2.7B vs. approximately $3B previously (due to slightly slower than expected rollout of some ad product capabilities). We anticipate an operating margin of 31.5% for 2026 (31.4% based on F/X rates as of January 1, 2026) vs. 29.5% in 2025. Our updated 2026 margin guidance includes ~30 basis points negative impact associated with our Q4 headcount reductions. Our forecast implies annual operating income growth of 20%+ for 2026.
exhibit-99-1.txt:66: Our Focus
exhibit-99-1.txt:67: Our mission is to entertain the world while building a wildly successful business. Our strategy is simple: invest in differentiated, exclusive, professionally-produced entertainment like Netflix originals that spark conversation, bring in more members, and make us a “must-have” service. We pair these originals, which anchor our service, with a broad, complementary selection of third-party programming, a great discovery experience, and leading global distribution. Together, this fuels engagement (quality, quantity, and variety of viewing) and, in turn, revenue and profit. The core of our service is streaming TV, film and live events, monetized via subscription and advertising. It represents the vast majority of our spending and nearly all of our revenue, and is the engine of our business for which we see a long runway of growth.
exhibit-99-1.txt:68: To successfully execute this strategy, we focus on three priorities: 1) delivering more entertainment value to our members, 2) leveraging technology to improve all aspects of our service, and 3) improving our monetization. These priorities work in concert to drive acquisition and retention, create member value that lets us occasionally raise prices, and increase advertiser demand. We reinvest returns in our business so we can win more moments of truth and fund the next wave of entertainment. Done well,

exhibit-99-1.txt:73: With intense competition and an explosion of content competing for consumer attention, strategic clarity and excellent execution are critical. In Q3, we delivered well across all three priorities, but we see room to do even better with focused, continuous improvement.

# Course operating rules

These are harness rules. They are not part of a role's identity, values, or scoring criteria.

- Use only the evidence included in the JSON hand-off.
- Put an exact filing-line citation or an exact `facts.json` citation immediately after every filing number.
- Put an exact `calculations.json` citation immediately after every code-calculated number.
- Do not use a web number in the graded report.
- Do not use a vendor-derived FAskills score in the graded report until every input is reproduced from SEC XBRL facts and the Verifier recomputes the score.
- Keep every period, condition, definition, and hedge supported by the source.
- Write `not stated in the supplied filings` when the supplied evidence does not state a value.
- Never calculate inside a model role.
- Preserve GAAP and adjusted labels.
- Name the denominator definition for every margin and peer comparison.
- In the Financial Analyst section, state the required claims with these exact lead phrases: `Annual total revenue was`; `Annual revenue growth was`; `Annual operating income was`; `Annual operating margin was`; `Annual net income attributable to the company was`; `Annual GAAP diluted EPS was`; `Return on average equity was`; `Debt to equity was`; `Free cash flow was`; `Quarter total revenue was`; `Quarter revenue growth was`; and `Quarter GAAP diluted EPS was`.
- Put each required claim on its own line. Do not add a second number to a required-claim line.
- Write citation tokens exactly, with no backticks and no space after the colon. Valid examples are `(10-k.txt:1294)`, `(facts.json:total_revenue)`, `(calculations.json:revenue_growth)`, `(peers.json:WMT:operating_margin)`, and `(manifest.json:price)`.
- Use one citation token for one source. Do not combine two source names inside one pair of parentheses.
- Do not write a numerical value unless its own exact citation token immediately follows it.
- Cite each peer operating margin as `(peers.json:TICKER:operating_margin)`.
- Cite the supplied share price as `(manifest.json:price)`.
- Give every numerical criterion score a same-line filing or calculation citation for the evidence used to assign that score.
- End each analyst output with one final nonblank line that begins exactly `Insight:`.
- The Insight must use exact supplied citation tokens and must not merely restate the earnings release's first paragraph.
- Do not write a four-digit year in an Insight unless the year has its own exact source citation.

# Overview

Netflix operates as a single-segment global entertainment service, deriving the vast majority of its revenue from monthly membership fees for streaming content, with a growing but currently non-material contribution from advertising, consumer products, and live experiences (10-k.txt:1721). The company’s core strategy is to grow globally within the parameters of its operating margin target, utilizing a range of pricing plans—including an ad-supported tier—to meet diverse consumer needs while continuously enhancing the user interface and content offerings (10-k.txt:1719). In fiscal year 2025, Netflix reported total revenues of $45,183,036 thousand, representing a 16% increase from $39,000,966 thousand in 2024 (10-k.txt:2058). Operating income expanded by 28% to $13,326,603 thousand, driving the operating margin up by 2.8 percentage points to 29.5% (10-k.txt:2061). This margin expansion was primarily driven by revenue growth outpacing the growth in cost of revenues, sales and marketing, and general and administrative expenses (10-k.txt:2069). Notably, the company discontinued the reporting of membership numbers and average monthly revenue per paying membership in 2025, shifting its primary financial metrics to revenue and operating margin (10-k.txt:2063).

**Criterion Scores:**
*   **Business-model durability:** 5. The model demonstrates strong durability, evidenced by a 29.5% operating margin in 2025, up from 26.7% in 2024 and 20.6% in 2023 (10-k.txt:2061). The shift to a multi-tier pricing model, including ad-supported plans, provides diversified revenue streams within the subscription base (10-k.txt:1719).
*   **Customer retention / Primary operating KPI:** 3. The company no longer discloses membership counts or churn rates in its 10-K, citing a focus on revenue and operating margin as primary metrics (10-k.txt:2063). While the Q3 2026 earnings release notes "continued, healthy retention in every region" and improved churn year-over-year (exhibit-99-1.txt:61), the absence of specific retention KPIs in the annual filing limits the ability to score this criterion highly based solely on the 10-K evidence.
*   **Organic growth:** 5. Revenue growth of 16% in 2025 was driven by memberships, price increases, and advertising revenue (10-k.txt:2080). Constant currency revenue growth was 17%, indicating strong underlying organic demand independent of foreign exchange fluctuations (10-k.txt:2059).
*   **Expansion-driven growth:** 4. Geographic expansion is evident in the revenue breakdown, with APAC growing 21% and EMEA growing 17% in 2025 (10-k.txt:2088). The company is also expanding its advertising tier to 15 new countries in 2027 (exhibit-99-1.txt:153).
*   **Competitive advantage:** 4. Netflix competes in an "intensely competitive" market against linear TV, other streaming providers, and social media (10-k.txt:1725). Its advantage lies in its global scale, proprietary content library, and technology infrastructure like Open Connect (10-k.txt:2109). The company states it strives to "win moments of truth" by continually improving service and content (10-k.txt:1726).
*   **Catalyst evidence:** 4. Catalysts include the expansion of the ad-supported tier to new markets, new licensing deals such as with Disney and TF1, and live events like NFL games and boxing matches (exhibit-99-1.txt:26). The company expects 2026 revenue of $51.1B and an operating margin of 31.5% (exhibit-99-1.txt:16).
*   **Moat risk:** 3. Risks include intense competition for consumer leisure time, regulatory changes in various countries that may increase operating costs or restrict content, and the need to continuously invest in content to maintain member engagement (10-k.txt:1725). The company acknowledges that it cannot provide assurance of prevailing in intellectual property disputes (10-k.txt:1730).

# Market Positioning and Growth Outlook

Netflix is positioned as a leading global entertainment service, competing for consumers' leisure time against a broad set of activities including linear television, other streaming providers, video gaming, and social media (10-k.txt:1725). The company’s strategy is to "win moments of truth" by offering compelling content and a superior user experience (10-k.txt:1726). In 2025, Netflix achieved significant geographic diversification, with UCAN contributing $19,957,152 thousand (15% growth), EMEA $14,514,646 thousand (17% growth), LATAM $5,357,521 thousand (11% growth), and APAC $5,353,717 thousand (21% growth) (10-k.txt:2087). The constant currency growth in LATAM was 23%, suggesting strong underlying demand in the region despite reported currency headwinds (10-k.txt:2102).

The company’s growth outlook is supported by its ability to raise prices and expand its advertising revenue. In Q3 2026, revenue grew 12% year-over-year to $12.9 billion, with operating margin reaching 34.6% (exhibit-99-1.txt:14). For full-year 2026, Netflix expects revenue of $51.1 billion, a 13% increase, and an operating margin of 31.5% (exhibit-99-1.txt:16). The company notes that member response to 2026 price changes has been consistent with prior adjustments, indicating healthy engagement and strong value perception (exhibit-99-1.txt:28). Additionally, the expansion of the advertising tier to 15 new countries in 2027, starting with nine EMEA countries, Colombia, Peru, and New Zealand in March 2027, provides a clear path for further revenue diversification (exhibit-99-1.txt:153).

**Criterion Scores:**
*   **Business-model durability:** 5. The model’s durability is reinforced by the 29.5% operating margin in 2025 and the projected 31.5% margin for 2026 (10-k.txt:2061). The company’s ability to maintain margin expansion while growing revenue at 16% demonstrates strong operational leverage (10-k.txt:2069).
*   **Customer retention / Primary operating KPI:** 3. While the 10-K does not provide specific retention metrics, the Q3 2026 earnings release highlights "continued, healthy retention in every region" and improved churn year-over-year (exhibit-99-1.txt:61). The company’s focus on engagement metrics, such as view hours, suggests a shift in how it measures customer value (exhibit-99-1.txt:157).
*   **Organic growth:** 5. The 17% constant currency revenue growth in 2025 indicates strong organic demand (10-k.txt:2059). The company’s ability to drive growth through price increases and advertising revenue, rather than solely relying on membership additions, supports the sustainability of this growth (10-k.txt:2080).
*   **Expansion-driven growth:** 4. The 21% growth in APAC and 17% growth in EMEA in 2025 highlight the company’s successful international expansion (10-k.txt:2088). The planned expansion of the ad-supported tier to new markets in 2027 further supports this growth vector (exhibit-99-1.txt:153).
*   **Competitive advantage:** 4. Netflix’s competitive advantage is underpinned by its global scale, proprietary content, and technology infrastructure. The company’s ability to secure licensing deals with major studios like Disney and TF1 demonstrates its attractiveness as a partner for content distribution (exhibit-99-1.txt:26).
*   **Catalyst evidence:** 4. Key catalysts include the launch of new ad-supported markets, new content partnerships, and live events. The company’s guidance for 2026 implies annual operating income growth of over 20% (exhibit-99-1.txt:65).
*   **Moat risk:** 3. The primary risks to the moat are intense competition and regulatory changes. The company notes that regulators in some countries are looking at restrictions that could require formal reviews of content, potentially increasing operating costs (10-k.txt:1732).

# Future Developments and Strategic Recommendations

Netflix’s future developments are centered on expanding its entertainment offering through licensing, new third-party content partnerships, and live events. The company has recently secured a licensing deal with Disney, bringing a variety of current and library series and films to its service, including the *Ice Age* films (exhibit-99-1.txt:129). Additionally, the partnership with TF1 in France allows Netflix to provide local series, film, news, and sports programming, generating incremental viewing in the region (exhibit-99-1.txt:152). The company is also investing in its ad tech stack, extending programmatic access through globally-available CTV marketplace deals and securing new partnerships with MercadoLibre in LATAM and AdForm in EMEA (exhibit-99-1.txt:153).

Strategically, Netflix is focusing on three priorities: delivering more entertainment value, leveraging technology to improve the service, and improving monetization (exhibit-99-1.txt:68). The company plans to introduce its advertising tier to 15 new countries in 2027, with the first tranche launching in March 2027 (exhibit-99-1.txt:153). This expansion is expected to drive further revenue growth and diversification. The company also anticipates that its 2026 operating margin of 31.5% will include a negative impact of approximately 30 basis points associated with Q4 headcount reductions, which are intended to enable continued investment in high-impact areas (exhibit-99-1.txt:65).

**Criterion Scores:**
*   **Business-model durability:** 5. The model’s durability is supported by the company’s ability to maintain high operating margins while expanding into new revenue streams such as advertising and live events (10-k.txt:2061).
*   **Customer retention / Primary operating KPI:** 3. The company’s focus on engagement metrics and its statement that member response to price changes is consistent with expectations suggest stable retention, but the lack of specific KPIs in the 10-K limits the score (10-k.txt:2063).
*   **Organic growth:** 5. The 17% constant currency revenue growth in 2025 and the expected 13% growth in 2026 indicate strong organic momentum (10-k.txt:2059).
*   **Expansion-driven growth:** 4. The expansion of the ad-supported tier to new markets and the growth in APAC and EMEA revenues support this score (10-k.txt:2088).
*   **Competitive advantage:** 4. Netflix’s competitive advantage is reinforced by its global scale, proprietary content, and technology infrastructure, as well as its ability to secure major licensing deals (exhibit-99-1.txt:26).
*   **Catalyst evidence:** 4. The launch of new ad-supported markets, new content partnerships, and live events provide clear catalysts for future growth (exhibit-99-1.txt:153).
*   **Moat risk:** 3. Risks include intense competition, regulatory changes, and the need to continuously invest in content to maintain member engagement (10-k.txt:1725).

Insight: The 23% constant currency revenue growth in LATAM (10-k.txt:2102) indicates that the company’s pricing and content strategy is resonating strongly in emerging markets, suggesting that the moat is being reinforced by successful localization and price optimization in regions with high growth potential.

# Course operating rules

These are harness rules. They are not part of a role's identity, values, or scoring criteria.

- Use only the evidence included in the JSON hand-off.
- Put an exact filing-line citation or an exact `facts.json` citation immediately after every filing number.
- Put an exact `calculations.json` citation immediately after every code-calculated number.
- Do not use a web number in the graded report.
- Do not use a vendor-derived FAskills score in the graded report until every input is reproduced from SEC XBRL facts and the Verifier recomputes the score.
- Keep every period, condition, definition, and hedge supported by the source.
- Write `not stated in the supplied filings` when the supplied evidence does not state a value.
- Never calculate inside a model role.
- Preserve GAAP and adjusted labels.
- Name the denominator definition for every margin and peer comparison.
- In the Financial Analyst section, state the required claims with these exact lead phrases: `Annual total revenue was`; `Annual revenue growth was`; `Annual operating income was`; `Annual operating margin was`; `Annual net income attributable to the company was`; `Annual GAAP diluted EPS was`; `Return on average equity was`; `Debt to equity was`; `Free cash flow was`; `Quarter total revenue was`; `Quarter revenue growth was`; and `Quarter GAAP diluted EPS was`.
- Put each required claim on its own line. Do not add a second number to a required-claim line.
- Write citation tokens exactly, with no backticks and no space after the colon. Valid examples are `(10-k.txt:1294)`, `(facts.json:total_revenue)`, `(calculations.json:revenue_growth)`, `(peers.json:WMT:operating_margin)`, and `(manifest.json:price)`.
- Use one citation token for one source. Do not combine two source names inside one pair of parentheses.
- Do not write a numerical value unless its own exact citation token immediately follows it.
- Cite each peer operating margin as `(peers.json:TICKER:operating_margin)`.
- Cite the supplied share price as `(manifest.json:price)`.
- Give every numerical criterion score a same-line filing or calculation citation for the evidence used to assign that score.
- End each analyst output with one final nonblank line that begins exactly `Insight:`.
- The Insight must use exact supplied citation tokens and must not merely restate the earnings release's first paragraph.
- Do not write a four-digit year in an Insight unless the year has its own exact source citation.
